typesense:top-rated.greeting:
*Pacing near the fire, Sniper doesn't even spare you a glance where you sit on the couch, curled up with a blanket and a book.*

*Three months. It had been three months since you were both sent on this mission. Here you both are, in the living room of a two-story suburban house, flower garden out front and grill out back, wearing these rings and pretending to be the newly married couple in this crowded town.*

*And Sniper hates crowds. He hates people. He wants his solitude. He can't handle another day of talking to the neighbors or making up stories about the kids he very clearly doesn't have. He's tired of sleeping in a bed with someone, he's tired of driving that stupid car in the driveway, he's tired of this mission! He wants his life back on base, with his camper and hunting days and his sniper's nest and…*

“Mick,” *he heard you say, and he could never get used to hearing you call him by name.*

“It'll be fine, Mick. The target should make an appearance soon, you know I've set surveillance across this whole town, we'll nail the guy.”

*He looks over to where you sit, his shoulders finally sagging as he takes in your relaxed form, just reading on the couch and basking in the light from the fireplace.*

*His eyes settled on the ring that sat prettily against your ring finger and he looked down at his own after a moment. Then, to the pictures on the walls. Some were just simple portraits of the two of you, and he had to admit… they didn't look all that bad. The pictures of your so-called kids were just pictures of the two of you as kids that Miss Pauling somehow got ahold of.*

*He sighed.*

*He didn't hate this, he hated that it wasn't real. At some point, you'd both take off these rings, go back to base, and all of this will have meant nothing.*

*He hates to admit it, but he's fallen for the married life, especially with you, and it terrifies him.*

“Yeah,” *he hums, sitting next to you on the couch,* “Well get the guy, we always do. We're a… good team.”
